name: boygenius
label: Interscope
lede: Three songwriters booked a tour before they had a song, recorded six in four days at Sound City, then took four years to make a record that went No. 1 in the U.K.

eras.title: Three rooms, three guitars
eras.text: Before there was a band there were three solo artists on the same circuit: Julien Baker recording alone in Memphis, Lucy Dacus finishing a debut in Virginia, Phoebe Bridgers taking meetings in Los Angeles. A 2016 run of opening slots put them in the same dressing rooms.

years.h: Sprained Ankle: Julien Baker's debut, recorded alone
years.p: Self-recorded and first shared on Bandcamp, then released by 6131 Records. Critics reached for words like "heartbreaking" and "hypnotic".
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the album as self-recorded, put up on Bandcamp first, and widely praised on release. Baker signed to Matador Records in 2017.

years.src: Rolling Stone: Boygenius on The Record · Exclaim!: The Magic of boygenius · Wikipedia: Julien Baker and Phoebe Bridgers with Lucy Dacus Tour
years.h: Lucy Dacus opens for Julien Baker in D.C. and they bond over Henry James
years.p: Dacus was the opener; Baker was reading, and remembers Dacus reading, The Portrait of a Lady. Bridgers, who opened for Baker on other dates, met her a month later.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone says Dacus and Baker met at the D.C. show and Baker met Bridgers a month after. Exclaim! puts the meeting in January 2016.

Wikipedia's account of the 2018 tour says Dacus and Bridgers each opened for Baker separately that year, and Baker introduced them to each other only in 2018.

years.h: No Burden: Lucy Dacus's debut lands her a Matador deal
years.p: Dacus had left the film program at Virginia Commonwealth University and worked as a photo editor. The record got her a contract with Matador.

years.src: Wikipedia: Better Oblivion Community Center · Wikipedia: Phoebe Bridgers
years.h: Bridgers meets Conor Oberst at a secret showcase in L.A.
years.p: At the Bootleg Theater, [[Conor Oberst|0eee89dc-7d86-4a15-97be-011652c49288]] heard she was a fan, invited her to play, then asked for her unreleased songs.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, Oberst suggested at the time that they "start a band and sound like the Replacements". Bridgers opened his European tour in 2017.

years.h: Stranger in the Alps: Bridgers's debut, on Dead Oceans
years.p: It came out to strong reviews and made her a name outside L.A. Tony Berg produced.

years.h: Turn Out the Lights: Baker adds strings and takes the Matador step
years.p: Recorded at Ardent Studios in Memphis with producer Calvin Lauber, with orchestral parts her debut didn't have.

eras.title: Six songs, four days, one tour already booked
eras.text: The idea was a seven-inch to sell at merch. Instead they booked the tour first, went to Sound City, and made six songs in four days that turned into a band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Julien Baker and Phoebe Bridgers with Lucy Dacus Tour · Exclaim!: The Magic of boygenius
years.h: They book a co-headlining tour before writing a note
years.p: Baker, Bridgers and Dacus put the dates on sale with no music written together. The plan was a single 7-inch for the merch table.
years.xp: Wikipedia's tour page says the trio booked the tour before recording anything. Exclaim! says the 7-inch was meant to sell at merch on a fall 2018 triple bill.

q: We set out to make one song, and made six.
years.src: Wikipedia: Boygenius (EP) · Wikipedia: Boygenius · Rolling Stone: Boygenius on The Record
years.h: Four days at Sound City, and every hire is a woman
years.p: The three self-produced at Sound City Studios in Van Nuys, California, and decided to hire only women for the sessions. Each brought one finished song and one unfinished idea.
years.xp: Wikipedia dates the recording to four days in June 2018. Bridgers described the plan to Rolling Stone this way: "We set out to make one song, and made six."

years.h: boygenius EP: Pitchfork 8.3, and a Matador stamp
years.p: Released two weeks ahead of the planned Nov. 9 date. Three songs had arrived Aug. 21: "Bite the Hand", "Me & My Dog", "Stay Down".
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the Pitchfork review at 8.3 (reviewer Dayna Evans) and Metacritic at 84. NPR Music ranked it 12th of 2018 despite the EP format, Wikipedia says.

years.src: Wikipedia: Julien Baker and Phoebe Bridgers with Lucy Dacus Tour · The Fader: boygenius tour and EP
years.h: Nashville's Ryman opens a November run that ends at the Wiltern
years.p: Each played a solo set; then all three took the stage for the EP. Nov. 4 to Nov. 30, Nashville to Los Angeles.
years.xp: Wikipedia and The Fader agree on the run, Nov. 4 to Nov. 30, 2018. The dates included Brooklyn Steel, Toronto's Danforth Music Hall, Chicago's Thalia Hall and Minneapolis's First Avenue.

years.src: NPR Music: boygenius Tiny Desk Concert
years.h: Tiny Desk: "Souvenir", "Me & My Dog", "Ketchum, ID"
years.p: NPR filmed the trio on Nov. 9; host Bob Boilen asked if it was any easier the second or third time. All three said no.
years.xp: Each had done a Tiny Desk alone before; Baker had done two. NPR published the video Nov. 15.

eras.title: Everybody goes solo, nobody quits
eras.text: The band went quiet, but not gone: backing vocals crossed over between each other's solo records, Bridgers made a second band with Conor Oberst, and one demo in a shared folder put it all back in motion.

years.h: Bridgers and Oberst surprise-release Better Oblivion Community Center
years.p: Their band debut came out through Dead Oceans and grew from the secret L.A. showcase where they met in 2016.

years.h: Punisher is Bridgers's second album; four Grammy nods follow
years.p: It earned her four nominations, including Best New Artist, at the 63rd Grammys. Dacus and Baker sing on tracks.

years.big: Can we be a band again?
q: Can we be a band again?
years.src: Rolling Stone: Boygenius on The Record · Exclaim!: The Magic of boygenius · Variety: boygenius record tour interview
yt: boygenius: Emily I'm Sorry (official music video)
years.h: The reunion starts with a demo in a shared folder
years.p: After Punisher, Bridgers put a demo of "Emily I'm Sorry" in front of the other two, with that question attached.
years.xp: Rolling Stone reports Bridgers's question, and Exclaim! places the shared-folder message after Punisher. Variety dates the album's origin to the week after Punisher.

years.h: They put the EP demos on Bandcamp and raise $23,000+
years.p: The money went to Downtown Women's Center in L.A., OUTMemphis and Mutual Aid Distribution Richmond.

years.h: Little Oblivions: Baker plays everything and lands in the top 40
years.p: Drums, bass, keyboards, mandolin and banjo, all Baker. It became her first Billboard 200 top-40 album.

years.h: First full show together since 2018: Bread and Roses benefit
years.p: They headlined the San Francisco benefit, three years after the tour that made them a band.

eras.title: The Record
eras.text: One month at Rick Rubin's studio, a deal with Interscope, three videos directed by Kristen Stewart, and a spring in which the debut album was No. 1 in the U.K. and No. 4 in the U.S.

years.cap: Shangri-La, Malibu, where most of the album was recorded in January 2022.
years.src: Rolling Stone: Boygenius on The Record · Wikipedia: The Record (Boygenius album) · Wikipedia: Not Strong Enough
years.h: A month inside Rick Rubin's Shangri-La in Malibu
years.p: Nearly all of January 2022, with co-producer Catherine Marks, plus Sound City in Van Nuys. Session players on "Not Strong Enough" included [[Jay Som|3b910f7b-018f-408f-950b-47e02d2ce305]] on bass and Carla Azar on percussion.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone puts the sessions at nearly all of January 2022 at [[Rick Rubin|07aebfa0-55d6-47e0-a284-12330e3eae0d]]'s Shangri-La. Wikipedia lists Sound City as the second studio, and Marks as co-producer.

Rolling Stone also says the album was the first major-label release for any of the three.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Record (Boygenius album) · Wikipedia: Boygenius
years.h: Three singles at once: "$20", "Emily I'm Sorry", "True Blue"
years.p: Music videos directed by Kristen Stewart, premiered together March 30 at the El Rey Theatre in Los Angeles.

years.h: "Not Strong Enough" arrives with a day-out-in-L.A. video
years.p: Filmed around Los Angeles County, edited by Bridgers's brother Jackson. It was the last song finished for the album.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the video shows the band spending a day together around Los Angeles County, including the Santa Monica Pier and the Getty Villa, and the song was the sixth of twelve tracks.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Record (Boygenius album) · Album of the Year: boygenius, the record · Rolling Stone: Boygenius on The Record
years.h: The Record: Pitchfork's 8.2, and No. 16 of 2023
years.p: Pitchfork's Cat Zhang gave it 8.2, and the site ranked it No. 16 on its year-end albums list. Interscope released it; Metacritic scores it 90.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists Pitchfork at 8.2 (Cat Zhang) and Metacritic at 90 from 26 critics. Album of the Year's aggregate is 88 from 40 reviews, and it ranks its own Pitchfork entry at 82.

Charts, per Wikipedia: No. 1 in the U.K., Ireland and the Netherlands, No. 4 on the Billboard 200. The cover echoes Crosby, Stills & Nash's debut, and Rolling Stone says the band's name refers to overconfident men praised for every thought.

years.src: Variety: boygenius record tour interview · Wikipedia: Boygenius
years.h: Coachella is the first big room for the new songs
years.p: Variety reported a warm-up show in Pomona before the festival. The tour ran April to August with Carly Rae Jepsen, Bartees Strange, Claud and others opening.
years.xp: Wikipedia adds Broken Social Scene and Illuminati Hotties to the openers, plus five fall dates with Palehound, Samia and Muna. Bridgers said it was "100 percent" their greatest tour experience.

years.h: Live at Pryzm in Kingston: "Emily I'm Sorry" into "Cool About It"
years.p: A U.K. date on the tour, captured on YouTube.

years.h: The Rest: four more songs, Pitchfork 7.5
years.p: "Black Hole", "Afraid of Heights", "Voyager", "Powers", cut in May 2023 at Blackbird in Tennessee and Sound City.
years.xp: It reached No. 50 on the Billboard 200, and No. 6 on Top Alternative Albums, per Wikipedia. Pitchfork called it aglow with the sense of triumph around the group's recent history.

years.src: Under the Radar: boygenius on SNL
years.h: Saturday Night Live, hosted by Timothée Chalamet
years.p: The band played and appeared in a sketch, the day after their Grammy nominations.

years.h: Year-end lists: No. 1 at NME, No. 2 at Rolling Stone
years.p: Variety and the Independent also put The Record first; Billboard put it second. Pitchfork ranked it No. 16.

eras.title: Hiatus, with three solo careers still running
eras.text: Two days before the Grammys, the band said it was going away for the foreseeable future. They won anyway, and the members are back on their own records.

years.src: Wikipedia: Boygenius · Stereogum: Boygenius Win Their First Grammy Awards
years.h: "We're going away for the foreseeable future"
years.p: At a small show at The Smell in Los Angeles, the band announced an indefinite hiatus, two days before the Grammys.
years.xp: NME quotes the band's message at that show: "We're going away for the foreseeable future. This is our last show, and we're feeling it." Per Wikipedia, Dacus said the final song was just the closing track, and she was "not convinced" the hiatus would be permanent.

years.src: Stereogum: Boygenius Win Their First Grammy Awards · NME: Boygenius' Julien Baker at 2024 Grammys · Wikipedia: Lucy Dacus · Wikipedia: Not Strong Enough
years.h: Three Grammys: Best Rock Song, Best Rock Performance, Best Alternative Album
years.p: "Not Strong Enough" won two, The Record won the third. Bridgers also won on SZA's "Ghost in the Machine".
years.xp:
Wikipedia describes the group as the first all-female band to win Best Rock Song and Best Rock Performance. "Not Strong Enough" lost Record of the Year to Miley Cyrus's "Flowers".

Baker told NME: "Music is the language I used to find my family since I was a kid."

years.h: Dacus's Forever Is a Feeling is her highest-charting solo album
years.p: Released on Geffen, it debuted at No. 16 on the Billboard 200.

years.h: Bridgers's third album, Lost Weekend, on Dead Oceans
years.p: Her first full solo album since Punisher in 2020.
